name: Tool-DE (Tool-Document Expansion); with Tool-Embed and Tool-Rank. Paper title: "Tools are under-documented: Simple Document Expansion Boosts Tool Retrieval"
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2510.22670, cs.IR), submitted 26 Oct 2025; no peer-reviewed venue identified as of research date [uncertain]
authors_affiliation: Xuan Lu, Haohang Huang, Rui Meng, Yaohui Jin, Wenjun Zeng, Xiaoyu Shen (corresponding). Affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Ningbo Key Laboratory of Spatial Intelligence and Digital Derivative; Institute of Digital Twin, Eastern Institute of Technology (EIT), Ningbo. Rui Meng noted working at Google Cloud AI Research.
code_url: https://github.com/EIT-NLP/Tool-DE (paper-listed; currently redirects to https://github.com/EIT-NLP/Tool-REX, the renamed maintained repo, ~10 stars, last pushed 2026-03)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/EIT-NLP/Tool-REX (renamed maintained repo for the Tool-DE benchmark, models, and training corpora)
task_domain: tool-use (tool retrieval / tool selection for LLM tool-augmented agents); information retrieval (cs.IR)
problem_setting: Offline, single-stage tool retrieval (and second-stage reranking) over a large static tool repository given a user query. The setting is non-interactive and supervised: query-tool relevance labels from 35 unified tool-use datasets are used to train a dense retriever and an LLM reranker. The core problem is a data-centric one: tool documentation is incomplete (~41.6% of audited docs lack a clear functional statement or usage guidance) and heterogeneous (up to seven phrasings for the same function), causing a semantic gap between user queries and tool docs. The proposed fix enriches each tool document with LLM-generated structured fields (query-independent, query-agnostic) before indexing/training.
what_is_retrieved: tools (tool/API documents). Retrieval targets enriched tool documentation (each tool doc augmented with a structured tool_profile containing function_description, when_to_use, limitations, tags; example_usage generated but excluded for retrieval after ablation).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed repository of ~43k tool documents (from ToolRet's 35 datasets) that is offline-expanded once with LLM-generated fields; no agent-written growing/episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking, but explicitly evaluated for multi-tool completeness: alongside NDCG@10 and Recall@10 they report Completeness@10 (C@K=1 only if ALL target tools for a query are in the top-K, else 0), targeting recovery of the complete needed set of tools per query rather than a single best tool.
retrieval_unit: tool-API document (a single tool/function document), each enriched with a structured tool_profile object; the retrieval unit is the whole expanded tool document, not a sub-span.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: built on ToolRet's 43k-tool corpus; tool docs are expanded once via an offline LLM pipeline (expansion -> judgement -> refinement -> human validation). Training corpora (50k for retriever, 200k for reranker) are also LLM-synthesized offline. No online/test-time index growth.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (dense embeddings) for the retriever; tool documents are structured internally into canonical/standardized fields (name, description, parameters, responses, method, category, example_usage, limitations) plus the added tool_profile, but the index itself is flat (no dependency graph or hierarchical category->tool topology used for retrieval).
retriever_type: hybrid coverage in experiments (sparse BM25s + dense embedding retrievers). The proposed model Tool-Embed is a dense retriever (fine-tuned Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B/4B); the second stage Tool-Rank is an LLM-based pointwise reranker (fine-tuned Qwen3-Reranker-4B).
retriever_learning_signal: Contrastive on similarity labels for the dense retriever: Tool-Embed is trained with InfoNCE loss on 50k query-tool pairs, with 5 in-batch random negatives sampled from other queries (full-parameter tuning, 1 epoch, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3). Tool-Rank is trained with a cross-entropy (pointwise true/false relevance) objective on 200k query-tool pairs via LoRA (r=32, alpha=64, dropout 0.1), 1 epoch. No RL or interactive preference signal.
query_construction: Raw user query plus a task-specific query instruction (instruction-style query as provided by ToolRet). Queries are NOT expanded/rewritten; the novelty is document-side expansion. The query-side stays as given (raw input + instruction).
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at retrieval time): a single query (with instruction) per retrieval task; no step/trajectory-level or two-level query construction.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (single retrieval pass per query), optionally followed by a single reranking pass over the top-100 candidates.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule / not applicable as a dynamic trigger: retrieval is performed once per query in a standard retrieve-then-rerank pipeline; there is no uncertainty- or confidence-based trigger and no agent-initiated retrieval request.
reranking: Yes. Two-stage pipeline: a dense retriever (Tool-Embed-4B) produces an initial candidate set, then a reranker reorders the top-100 candidates. Proposed reranker Tool-Rank-4B is an LLM-based pointwise reranker that outputs true/false logits normalized into P(relevant|q,d) as the reranking score. Off-the-shelf rerankers (jina-reranker-m0, bge-reranker-v2-gemma, Qwen3-Reranker-4B) are also evaluated.
retrieved_context_refinement: Document-side, pre-index refinement rather than post-retrieval: tool documents are enriched (document expansion) and canonicalized/standardized before indexing. Post-retrieval, a reranking stage refines ordering. No reason-in-documents distillation or distractor filtering of retrieved context is applied to the query-time results beyond reranking.
how_retrieved_used: Not used as in-context exemplars for downstream agent reasoning in this paper; retrieval/reranking is the end task. The enriched documents are used as (a) the indexed/retrievable content, (b) training signal for the retriever and reranker, and (c) the candidate documents scored by the reranker. Output is a ranked list of tools intended to be passed to a downstream tool-using agent (downstream agent usage is motivational, not evaluated here).
planning_integration: retrieve-then-(re)rank pipeline; not integrated into a multi-step planning/acting loop. Retrieval is the gateway to tool use but the paper evaluates retrieval quality in isolation (no MCTS/tree-search/per-step planning integration).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-query (single retrieval + single rerank pass per query); no per-CoT-step or per-tool-call interleaving. The reranker's prompt includes empty <think></think> tags (reasoning disabled) following Lu et al. 2025.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured note / enriched document: a tool document presented as the original documentation merged with a structured tool_profile (function_description, when_to_use, limitations, tags). Surface form is text JSON-style fields, not raw trajectories or executable programs.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single tool documentation entry enriched to a standardized profile (a tool-API description with explicit functional, situational, and constraint signals). It is a document/tool-API unit, more abstract/standardized than a raw docstring but not a distilled multi-step strategy or workflow.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Pipeline-level faithfulness controls plus an emergent separability effect. (1) Construction-time: rule-based JSON validation + LLaMa-3.1-70B faithfulness judgement + GPT-4o refinement for the ~1.5% failing cases + human validation (100 sampled profiles, all passed), preventing hallucinated/unsupported fields. (2) Evaluation-time: document expansion lowers absolute similarity but asymmetrically (negatives drop more than positives), sharpening positive/negative separability and improving robustness of ranking. No retriever-aware distractor SFT beyond standard negative sampling.
memory_type: none (static document store; no episodic / skill-library / procedural / graph / latent memory that grows from agent experience).
write_back: No. The system does not store new experiences/cases at deployment; the only writing is the one-time offline document expansion into the corpus and synthesis of training data.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store is frozen after offline document expansion; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: Never (no runtime write-back). Document enrichment occurs once offline via the expansion->judgement->refinement->human-validation pipeline, not triggered by task success/failure or reflection at inference.
failure_experience_usage: Not applicable / success-oriented only. No storage or retrieval of failed/negative agent experiences. The only failure handling is in the construction pipeline: profiles failing the judgement step (~1.5%) are regenerated/refined with GPT-4o. Training uses random negatives for contrastive learning but not stored failure trajectories.
memory_evolution_update: Append-and-refine at construction time only: original doc is unioned with the generated tool_profile (d_expansion = d_original ∪ d_profile); failing profiles are refine-overwritten via GPT-4o. No post-deployment mutation of stored entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No (not an RL/learned-policy retrieval). Retrieval is similarity-based dense top-k (contrastively trained embedder) plus a pointwise relevance-classifier reranker; selection is not a sequential decision policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single static shared corpus consumed by retrievers/rerankers; no multi-agent or cross-framework experience sharing.
benchmarks: ToolRet (Shi et al. 2025) and Tool-DE (this paper's document-expanded benchmark built on ToolRet). Both span three domains: Web (APIs), Code (functions), Customized (apps). Tool-DE is built from 35 well-established tool-use datasets unified by ToolRet; ~7.6k retrieval tasks over ~43k tools. Released training corpora: Tool-Embed-Train (50k) and Tool-Rank-Train (200k).
benchmark_family: tool (tool retrieval): ToolRet / Tool-DE. Underlying source datasets include ToolBench, APIBank, MetaTool, ToolACE, Gorilla, CRAFT, TaskBench, ToolAlpaca, etc.
baselines: Sparse: BM25s. Dense retrievers: GritLM-7B, NV-Embed-v1, gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct, e5-mistral-7b-instruct, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B/4B/8B. LLM-based rerankers: jina-reranker-m0, bge-reranker-v2-gemma, Qwen3-Reranker-4B. Also the paper's own non-expansion-trained counterparts Tool-Embed_original-0.6B/4B and Tool-Rank_original-4B. Reference SoTA: Qwen3-Embedding-8B (MTEB open-source SoTA as of 2025-09-20).
key_metrics: NDCG@10 (N@10), Recall@10 (R@10), Completeness@10 (C@10, all-target-tools-in-top-K = 1 else 0). Reported per domain (Web/Code/Customized) and averaged.
headline_result: On Tool-DE, the full pipeline (Tool-Embed-4B retriever + Tool-Rank-4B reranker) achieves NDCG@10 = 56.44, Recall@10 = 67.81, Completeness@10 = 56.60 (Avg.), i.e., +10.23 / +10.29 / +9.08 over the MTEB open-source SoTA Qwen3-Embedding-8B. Tool-Rank-4B improves the first-stage Tool-Embed-4B by +4.21 NDCG@10 (52.23 -> 56.44).
ablations: (1) Per-field Add-One vs One-Out analysis (GritLM dense + BM25s sparse, NDCG@10): example_usage gives smallest/often negative gains and even hurts GritLM; removing it (One-Out) raises N@10, so example_usage is excluded and function_description, when_to_use, limitations, tags are retained. function_description and tags are neutral-to-positive in Add-One and their removal causes notable drops in One-Out. (2) Document expansion as training signal: expansion-trained Tool-Embed-0.6B/4B gain +4.97/+6.69 over Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B baseline vs +3.69/+3.67 for non-expansion Tool-Embed_original; Tool-Rank gains +4.21 vs +2.00 for Tool-Rank_original. Gains persist even on non-expanded ToolRet test docs (generalization). (3) Evaluation-time similarity analysis (GritLM, 300 queries): expansion lowers similarities but negatives drop more than positives (e.g., Customized positives -0.0027 vs negatives -0.0152), sharpening separability. (4) Controlled toggle (fixed retrieval pool, switching expanded vs non-expanded document views) confirms removing expansions sharply attenuates reranker improvements. (5) Incompleteness audit: 41.6% of docs incomplete before expansion, dropping to 23.5% after.
evaluation_decoupling: Retrieval is the end task here, so all reported metrics are intrinsic IR metrics (NDCG@10, Recall@10, Completeness@10); there is no separate end-to-end downstream agent task metric. Thus retrieval quality is fully decoupled but no separate downstream task accuracy is reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome (ranking quality) metrics only: NDCG/Recall/Completeness@10. No reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise process metrics (reranker reasoning is explicitly disabled with empty <think></think>).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Construction cost emphasized as low: a four-stage pipeline using mid-sized open models (Qwen3-32B for expansion, LLaMa-3.1-70B for judgement) and GPT-4o only for the ~1.5% failing cases; profile adds modest length (avg original doc 131.72 tokens + tool_profile 45.89 -> expanded 177.61 tokens). Training on two NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, 1 epoch each. Efficiency point: Tool-Embed-0.6B outperforms baselines up to 8B params (smaller model, better accuracy). No explicit latency/throughput numbers reported [uncertain on per-query latency].
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k evaluation at K=10 (NDCG/Recall/Completeness@10). Reranking operates on the top-100 retrieved candidates per query. Added context per tool is budget-light (avg +45.89 tokens via tool_profile; total avg expanded doc 177.61 tokens). Note the analysis flags truncation risk: longer expanded inputs can dilute salient signals / be truncated under retriever token budgets.
builds_on: ToolRet benchmark (Shi et al. 2025) as the underlying corpus/datasets; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B/4B (retriever base) and Qwen3-Reranker-4B (reranker base) (Zhang et al. 2025); InfoNCE contrastive training; ms-swift and LLaMA-Factory training frameworks; document/query expansion lineage (Query2doc, EnrichIndex). Reranking prompt follows Lu et al. 2025 (Rethinking reasoning in document ranking).
contrasts_with: Query-side / work-around approaches that do not fix documentation at the source: Re-Invoke (LLM pseudo-queries + intent extraction), EASYTOOL (restructure docs into concise instructions), MassTool (multi-task search-based retrieval with intent modeling), ScaleMCP (dynamic weighting of document segments), MCP-Zero, TURA. The paper argues these work around poor documentation, whereas Tool-DE fixes the root cause by standardizing and completing tool documentation via offline document expansion.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): tool retrieval / tool-document engineering line. Sits in the 2024-2025 tool-retrieval sub-topic emphasizing tool_document_engineering (document expansion) and index standardization; descends from classic IR query/document expansion (Query2doc, EnrichIndex) applied to tool retrieval, contrasting with query-side expansion (Re-Invoke) and dynamic-index/MCP works (ScaleMCP, MCP-Zero).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method): [Retrieve] partial (tool retrieval), [Reuse] N/A, [Revise] N/A, [Retain] N/A.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is a document-expansion / tool-retrieval framework.
tool_document_engineering: Core contribution: LLM-driven synthetic document expansion. Each raw tool doc is enriched with a structured tool_profile via Qwen3-32B (reasoning mode), generating function_description and tags (always) plus when_to_use, limitations, example_usage (only if explicitly supported by the doc; query-independent, strictly grounded, unsupported fields omitted). Faithfulness ensured by LLaMa-3.1-70B judgement, GPT-4o refinement, and human validation. After ablation, example_usage is dropped; function_description, when_to_use, limitations, tags are retained. Also includes canonicalization of heterogeneous raw field names into 8 unified fields (name, description, category, parameters, responses, method, example_usage, limitations). This is expanded-summary / synthetic-field augmentation, not raw docstring use.
index_content_separation: No explicit lightweight-index-then-heavy-content (progressive disclosure) mechanism. The expanded document is embedded/indexed in full; there is no separation of a lightweight retrievable index from on-demand-loaded heavy content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static index (offline-expanded, frozen). No live tool synchronization, no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling auto-sync CRUD (the paper contrasts itself with ScaleMCP's dynamic auto-synchronizing MCP tools but does not implement such live sync).
tool_dependency_awareness: No. Retrieval does not model inter-tool dependencies (no dependency graph, bipartite KG, or dependency-aware reranking). Completeness@10 measures multi-tool coverage per query but tools are scored independently; prerequisite/output-feeds-input relations are not modeled.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR case adaptation). The closest analogue is offline document refinement (GPT-4o regeneration for failing profiles), but retrieved items are not adapted to the query at inference.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a benchmark+framework+models paper, not a survey/taxonomy).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Tool-DE is LLM-synthesized document expansion applied on top of ToolRet: built from 35 well-established tool-use datasets, ~7.6k retrieval tasks over a ~43k-tool corpus, across Web/Code/Customized domains. Construction: four-stage pipeline (expansion via Qwen3-32B, judgement via LLaMa-3.1-70B, GPT-4o refinement for ~1.5%/~600 failing cases, human validation of 100 profiles all passing). Released training corpora: Tool-Embed-Train (50k retriever instances) and Tool-Rank-Train (200k reranker instances). Answer verifiability via labeled ground-truth target tools (NDCG/Recall/Completeness@10). Difficulty signal: best system (Tool-Embed-4B + Tool-Rank-4B) reaches only 56.44 NDCG@10 Avg., indicating substantial headroom.
